back: Do not overstate profit or assets; recognise expected losses, but profits only when realised.
Revenue is recognised when earned (goods delivered), not when cash is received.
Expenses are charged in the period in which they help to earn revenue.
An item is material if omitting or misstating it could change users' decisions.
The same accounting methods are used each period unless a change is justified and disclosed.
The assumption that the business will continue for the foreseeable future.
Record the economic reality of a transaction, not just its legal form (for example a finance lease).
Estimated selling price less costs still to be incurred to complete and sell.
Lower of cost and net realisable value, item by item.
